residual_risk: Adopters who already ran hkb init keep the old block; their next init appends only the pidfile line, but a pidfile already committed stays committed until they git rm --cached it. Nothing warns about that — hkb doctor could, and does not.
The superset guard only runs in this repo, so it protects the shipped list against hkb-side drift, not against a .kanban/ path added without touching either file.

results.summary: `hkb init` now writes `.kanban/dispatch.pid` into .gitignore. The list moved to an exported GITIGNORE_LINES in src/init.js and ensureGitignore is exported; test/init.test.js (new, 5 tests) asserts both directions of the drift that caused this — hkb's own .gitignore is a superset of what init ships, and no .kanban/ path ignored here goes unshipped (board.json excepted, it is the tracked one). I diffed the rest of the list against this repo's .gitignore: dispatch.pid was the only entry missing. Two smaller things: presence is compared per trimmed line so a CRLF .gitignore stays idempotent instead of re-appending the block on every init, and the README's 'Local state (gitignored)' section now lists all seven paths instead of four. Draft PR #77.
